# Token Efficiency Benchmarks

Published compression ratios, token count comparisons, and accuracy
measurements for structured data formats in LLM contexts. All claims cite
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Benchmark Sources

Five independent sources provide token efficiency data. They differ in
methodology, models tested, and measurement granularity:

| Source | Formats Tested | Models | Measurement | Tier |
|--------|---------------|--------|-------------|------|
| TOON official [2] | TOON, JSON, JSON compact, YAML, XML, CSV | 4 LLMs | Tokenizer (o200k_base) | 2 |
| Piotr Sikora [11] | TOON, TRON, JSON, YAML, CSV | N/A | Character/token approx | 3 |
| JTON paper [12] | JTON, TOON, JSON compact | 10 LLMs | Tokenizer | 1 (preprint) |
| Spring AI [13] | TOON, JSON, YAML, XML, CSV | 1 LLM | API token counts | 3 |
| Microsoft [14] | JSON, YAML, function calling | GPT-4o | API token counts | 3 |

## Token Savings vs JSON

### Consolidated Rankings

Savings percentages vary by data shape, benchmark, and baseline. The table
below shows the range across sources:

| Format | vs JSON (pretty-print) | vs JSON (compact) | Best Source |
|--------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| CSV | 50–80% (cost projection [11]) | 58.8% [2] | Flat tabular only |
| TOON | 35–46% [2][11] | 13–22% [2][12] | Mixed/tabular data |
| TRON | ~31% avg token savings [11] | Not independently measured | Uniform arrays |
| YAML | 30–41% [11][14] | ~30% completion tokens [14] | Nested structures |
| JTON | 32.2% avg [12] | 20.2% [12] | JSON-compatible alternative |
| XML | −13% to −45% [2][13] | Worse than JSON | Consistently worst |

### The TOON "39.9%" Claim

The TOON benchmark page states "TOON achieves 76.4% accuracy (vs JSON's
75.0%) while using 39.9% fewer tokens" [2]. This figure requires context:

- **39.9% is vs standard (pretty-printed) JSON**, not compact JSON [2]
- **Mixed-structure track vs JSON:** −21.9% (TOON 227,830 vs JSON 291,711) [2]
- **Mixed-structure track vs JSON compact:** TOON uses **more** tokens
  (227,830 vs 198,546) [2]
- **Independent measurement (JTON paper):** TOON achieves −19.2% vs JSON
  compact across 6 datasets [12]
- **Creator's own claim in interviews:** "~40% fewer tokens" [32][39]

The 39.9% figure is accurate for the comparison stated but does not apply
to compact JSON, which is the format most agent systems actually use. Against
compact JSON, TOON's advantage is 13–22% on mixed data and disappears
entirely on flat-only data (+5.9% vs CSV) [2].

### TRON Compression

TRON data comes primarily from one source [11]:

- **Piotr Sikora:** ~31% average token savings across scenarios; 60% figure
  is a cost projection at 10K records with GPT-4 pricing, not direct
  compression [11]
- **No official TRON benchmarks found** — the TRON website playground requires
  JavaScript rendering and no static benchmark document exists [4]
- TRON's class syntax is most effective on **arrays of uniform objects** where
  property name repetition is highest (e.g., RAG chunks: −38% vs JSON) [11]
- On flat data or data with variable schemas, savings are lower [11]

### YAML vs JSON

Multiple independent sources confirm YAML's advantage:

- **Microsoft study:** 30% fewer completion tokens (260 vs 370) on GPT-4o [14]
- **Piotr Sikora:** 41% overall savings vs JSON [11]
- **ImprovingAgents:** YAML consistently highest accuracy for GPT-5 Nano
  (62.1%) and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (51.9%) [15]
- **Spring AI:** YAML 928 total tokens vs JSON 992 (7% savings) on small
  dataset [13]

### CSV as Upper Bound

CSV achieves the highest compression for flat tabular data (50–80% vs JSON)
[11] but cannot represent nested structures [2][10][13]. It serves as a
theoretical upper bound for tabular data efficiency.

## LLM Comprehension Accuracy

### Does Format Affect Accuracy?

| Source | Finding | Models |
|--------|---------|--------|
| TOON benchmark [2] | TOON 76.4% vs JSON 75.0% vs JSON compact 73.7% | 4 models |
| JTON paper [12] | JTON +0.3pp vs JSON; 3 of 10 models regressed | 10 models |
| ImprovingAgents [15] | Model-dependent: YAML best for GPT-5 Nano, JSON best for Llama 3.2 3B | 3 models |

Key findings:
- **Format preference is model-dependent** [15]. No single format dominates
  across all models.
- **TOON's accuracy advantage over JSON is marginal** (1.4pp on TOON's own
  benchmark) [2] and not independently replicated.
- **GPT-5.1 regressed −8.6pp** on JTON's Zen Grid vs JSON [12], showing that
  newer/larger models do not always handle alternative formats better.
- **XML consistently underperforms** on accuracy across all sources [2][15].

### Per-Model Variance (TOON Benchmark)

| Model | TOON | JSON | JSON compact | Spread |
|-------|------|------|-------------|--------|
| claude-haiku-4-5 | 59.8% | 57.4% | 55.0% | 4.8pp |
| gemini-3-flash | 96.7% | 97.1% | 96.7% | 0.4pp |
| gpt-5-nano | 90.9% | 89.0% | 90.9% | 1.9pp |
| grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | 58.4% | 56.5% | 52.2% | 6.2pp |
[2]

On high-capability models (Gemini 3 Flash), format makes almost no
difference (0.4pp spread). On weaker models (Grok-4.1-fast), the spread
widens to 6.2pp [2].

## Structured Output Generation

The JTON paper tested whether LLMs can **generate** alternative formats
(not just read them). Key finding: **100% syntactic validity** across 12
models for both few-shot and zero-shot JTON generation [12]. Models tested
include GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Llama 3.3
70B [12]. TOON generation was not tested in this study.

## Cost Impact at Scale

Piotr Sikora's cost projections at 10K records with GPT-4 pricing [11].
**Note:** These percentages reflect cost savings at scale, which compound
token savings with record density improvements. They are larger than direct
token compression ratios (e.g., TOON 75% cost savings vs 35% avg token
savings) [11]:

| Format | Cost per Call | Annual (1M calls) | vs JSON |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
| JSON | $5.60 | $5.6M | baseline |
| YAML | $3.33 | $3.3M | −41% |
| TRON | $2.24 | $2.2M | −60% |
| TOON | $1.38 | $1.4M | −75% |
| CSV | $1.14 | $1.1M | −80% |
[11]

**Caveat:** These projections use character counts and token approximations,
not verified API token measurements [11]. The actual savings depend on data
shape, model tokenizer, and whether compact or pretty-printed JSON is the
baseline.

## Context Window Capacity

At 128K token context window, approximate record capacity [11]:

| Format | Records | Multiplier vs JSON |
|--------|---------|-------------------|
| JSON | ~17K | 1× |
| YAML | ~29K | 1.7× |
| TRON | ~45K | 2.6× |
| TOON | ~70K | 4.1× |
| CSV | ~85K | 5.0× |
[11]

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No peer-reviewed token efficiency study** exists for TOON or TRON as of
  April 2026. The JTON paper [12] is the closest but is itself a preprint.
- **TOON benchmarks are self-reported** by the project creator's
  organization [2]. Independent measurements (JTON paper, Spring AI) show
  lower savings than the headline 39.9% claim [12][13].
- **TRON has no independently verified benchmarks** — all data comes from
  one practitioner blog post using character-count approximations [11].
- **Measurement methodology varies widely:** tokenizer-based counts [2][12]
  vs API token counts [13][14] vs character approximations [11]. These are
  not directly comparable.
- **TOON benchmark uses cutting-edge models** (GPT-5 Nano, Grok-4.1) [2]
  that may not represent typical production environments.
